about: Real official headlines (GOV.UK departments and NCSC), 28 Jun to 28 Sep 2026, chosen because they touch the words the automatic level rules look for. Open Government Licence / NCSC public feed. 3,566 headlines were checked in total.

items.title: FCDO summons Iranian Chargé d'Affaires over attack on Iran international journalist
items.summary: The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office has today summoned the Iranian Chargé d'Affaires in London in response to the sentencing of two individuals for their role in the attack on an Iran International journalist in 2024.
items.source: GOV.UK: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

items.title: Russia is using civilian suffering as a coercive tool: UK statement to the OSCE
items.summary: Ambassador Holland condemned Russia’s intensified missile and drone strikes on Ukrainian cities, highlighting civilian casualties and damage to humanitarian infrastructure. Russia has rejected opportunities for a ceasefire and is using continued attacks to exert pressure.
items.source: GOV.UK: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

items.title: FCDO summons Iranian Chargé d'Affaires over Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Qods Force’s role in directing attacks by proxy groups
items.summary: The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office has today summoned the Iranian Chargé d'Affaires in London in response to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Qods Force’s (IRGC-QF) role in directing proxy groups to carry out a series of attacks across Europe.
items.source: GOV.UK: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

items.title: Prime Minister commits €300 million to fund fighter jets for Ukraine - backing British jobs and bolstering Ukraine’s defence
items.summary: Prime Minister Keir Starmer has today announced that the UK is investing €300 million to help deliver advanced Swedish Gripen fighter jets to Ukraine, strengthening Ukraine’s ability to defend its skies from Russian attacks, while supporting thousands of highly skilled jobs across the UK.

items.title: Russia’s aggression is the root cause of insecurity: UK statement to the OSCE
items.summary: Ambassador Holland said Russia alone caused this war through its illegal use of force against Ukraine. NATO and international support for Ukraine are defensive responses to Russian aggression. Russia should stop attacks, accept a ceasefire and pursue a just, lasting peace.
items.source: GOV.UK: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

items.title: First groups designated as threat to national security
items.summary: The IRGC, IMCR, and the GRU Volunteer Corps have now been formally designated as threats to national security under new state threats powers.

items.title: Russia’s aerial attacks increase the risk of wider escalation: UK statement to the OSCE
items.summary: UK Senior Military Adviser, Colonel Joby Rimmer, warns that Russia’s missile and drone attacks endanger civilians, violate neighbouring states’ airspace and increase the risk of miscalculation and escalation across Europe.
items.source: GOV.UK: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

items.title: ODIHR’s latest report adds to the growing evidence of Russia’s contemptible conduct in Ukraine: UK statement to the OSCE
items.summary: The UK condemned Russia’s ongoing aerial attacks on Ukraine and cited ODIHR’s latest report which shows evidence of civilian harm, arbitrary detention and efforts to erase Ukrainian identity in the temporarily occupied territories.
items.source: GOV.UK: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

items.title: UK pledges winter air defence package to boost Ukraine's defences
items.summary: The UK will supply air defence interceptors, large-calibre artillery rounds and drones to help Ukraine defend itself against barbaric Russian attacks this winter, as part of Britain’s commitment to help Ukraine defend its freedom and sovereignty.

items.title: A negotiated settlement is the only long-term solution to the threat posed by Iran’s nuclear programme: UK statement at the UN Security Council
items.summary: Statement by Ambassador Sarah MacIntosh, UK Permanent Representative to the UN, at the UN Security Council meeting on Iran.
items.source: GOV.UK: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

items.title: Responsible technology and resilience against hybrid threats: UK statement to the 32nd OSCE Economic and Environmental Forum
items.summary: Ambassador Holland highlights responsible governance and multistakeholder cooperation are essential to harness frontier technologies while protecting human rights and public trust. The OSCE must strengthen early warning, address hybrid threats and support Ukraine’s recovery and resilience in the face of Russia’s illegal war.
items.source: GOV.UK: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

items.title: UK and allies expose spyware used by Iranian state actors to target dissidents, activists and journalists

items.title: On the incident at Leipzig airport on 4th August: UK statement to the OSCE
items.summary: Ambassador Holland expresses UK solidarity with Germany following Russia's reckless hybrid actions.
items.source: GOV.UK: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

items.title: Russia’s intensified attacks on Ukraine and their wider consequences: UK statement to the OSCE
items.summary: Ambassador Holland highlights evidence that Russia has intensified its attacks on Ukraine, causing severe harm to civilians, infrastructure, trade and food security. The UK says sustained support for Ukraine and pressure on Russia should lead to serious negotiations and a just, lasting peace based on OSCE principles.
items.source: GOV.UK: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

items.title: Russia’s threat extends beyond Ukraine: UK statement to the OSCE
items.summary: UK Senior Military Advisor, Joby Rimmer, condemns Russia’s attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport and its intensified campaign against Ukraine, and calls for a just and lasting peace.
items.source: GOV.UK: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

items.title: Cyber Security Breaches Survey (CSBS) 2026/2027
items.summary: The Cyber Security Breaches Survey (CSBS) is an annual UK Official Statistics publication that provides a comprehensive picture of cyber resilience, threats, breaches and attacks experienced by businesses, charities, and educational institutions, helping to inform government cyber security policy.

items.title: Russia is widening insecurity while refusing the path to peace: UK statement to the OSCE
items.summary: Counsellor for Politico-Military Affairs, Arron Newble, says Russia’s intensified attacks on Ukraine and disruptive activity across Europe are not evidence of success, and calls on Russia to agree an immediate ceasefire and engage seriously in negotiations towards a just and lasting peace.
items.source: GOV.UK: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
